name: ual_parse
description: Read a Microsoft 365 unified audit log export offline (portal or PowerShell CSV with an AuditData column, JSON with that wrapper, native audit events as an array, JSON Lines or a value envelope, a Graph audit log record) and open the payload: `audit_data` is the whole AuditData as written (Name/Value, NewValue/OldValue and duplicate parameter names kept), beside the lifted fields (operation, user, address, workload, record type, result, record id, MailAccessType, OperationCount, items listed) and each record's file, record and line. `status` and `status_basis` say whether every row was read; a row that is not an audit record, a payload that is not JSON (kept with its outer columns), a file that is not an audit export, a CSV line past the field limit, an archive (.zip, tar: named, not read), a next-page marker, an export whose own ResultCount says more records matched than it holds, and files not reached before the time limit are counted separately, located and listed. Time: AuditData's CreationTime, else the outer column; no zone is not UTC unless assume_utc says so (a native CreationTime with no zone included, and a row left undated says so in time_zone), a day/month/year string needs a date_order or unambiguous rows that prove one (reported), and a declared date_order that a row contradicts leaves that row undecoded, named; raw and decoded times are kept; since/until exclude rows whose time could not be read and count them (status is then partial). record_type matches the payload's RecordType and the outer column, by number or by name as the export wrote them (the export's own pairing is shown in record_types_all_rows; no number-to-name table is built in), and a filter value that matched no row is reported. Summary tables describe the matched records; operations_all_rows and record_types_all_rows are every row, withheld the same way. `user` is a regex (at most 200 characters) matched against the user as printed, never against a withheld original; a pattern that can take exponential time is refused, and one test that takes more than a quarter of a second fails the call, named. An argument the tool does not have is refused. `notable` names an operation, not its meaning: MailItemsAccessed is not a statement that content was read. NOT measured: whether the audit configuration or licence captured every operation (aggregation and duplicate suppression can apply: check the schema the export carries), or who a record's user is. SENSITIVE: parameters and properties can hold secrets; a field named or shaped like a credential is withheld and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT; run as a job with secret_output: true. An out_file is never replaced by a smaller result; a read that ended early publishes it as <name>.partial<ext> and names it partial_records, never complete_records, and SIGTERM leaves no temporary file.

path.description: An export (CSV, JSON, JSON Lines; the format is read from the content) or a directory of them

operations.description: Keep only these operations (compared without case, as printed; a value that matched nothing is reported as given)

user.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the user as printed; a pattern that can take exponential time is refused

since.description: ISO 8601 lower bound (a bound with no zone is UTC); a row whose time could not be read is excluded and counted

until.description: ISO 8601 upper bound (a bound with no zone is UTC)

record_type.description: Keep only these record types: the number or the name, matched against the payload's RecordType and the outer column as the export wrote them, without case or white space and a number without leading zeros (no built-in table pairs a number with a name; a value that matched nothing is reported as given)

notable_only.description: Only the operations this tool lists for a second look

assume_utc.description: Read a time that carries no zone as UTC. Say so only on the export's own documentation or collection record; each record's time_status says it was assumed

date_order.description: mdy or dmy, for day/month/year strings whose two leading fields are both 12 or less

format.description: auto (default: from the content), csv or json

delimiter.description: CSV delimiter, one character (default a comma)

max_field_bytes.description: Longest CSV line read (default 64 MiB); a longer one stops the file, named, with what was read kept

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for every matching record, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Never replaces a file already there: that one is kept and this one is named beside it

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); past it the whole list is in a file the answer names (under $OUT/tool-output in a job, work/<agent>/tool-output otherwise)

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 540, at most 580); what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. Honoured only when the tool runs as a job (run it with secret_output: true); outside a job it is refused and nothing is written
